subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme: Post-call TCO recap + next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of the pain, goals, and the cost levers we discussed, plus a couple of concrete next steps. I attached a 1‑page TCO summary and a sample pricing sheet for quick reference.

Quick recap (pain & goals)
- Pain: customer support chat volume driving unpredictable token costs; latency spikes during peak hours; engineering bandwidth constrained for inference ops.
- Goals: predictably manage monthly inference spend, keep 99th‑pct latency under ~300ms for chat use cases, and preserve output quality while hitting budget targets.

Key levers we discussed (how Redwood helps)
1) Model mix: route high‑throughput omnichannel flows to smaller, optimized models (2.7B) and reserve larger models (13B) for complex flows — immediately reduces per‑token compute.
2) Batching & continuous batching: increases GPU throughput and reduces per‑token served cost (typical throughput gain 20–40% depending on request parallelism).
3) KV/prefix caching: for session-based chat, avoid recomputing repeated context — can reduce effective prompt tokens by ~20–30% for multi-turn flows.
4) Quantization & runtime kernels: safe INT8 paths for many open models to lower GPU memory and increase density.
5) Dedicated/reserved capacity: commit pricing for predictable budget and lower unit costs vs pay‑as‑you‑go.

Initial ballpark TCO (very rough)
- Assumptions: 500k monthly sessions; average session = 120 input tokens + 400 output tokens => ~520 tokens/session => ~260M tokens/month.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) example: $3.00 per 1M tokens => 260 * $3 = $780/month (raw compute cost example).
- With batching + caching (expected ~40% combined savings) => effective tokens ≈ 156M => ~156 * $3 = $468/month.
- Dedicated reserved (12‑month commit) can reduce unit to ~$2.00 per 1M => 156 * $2 = $312/month.
- ROI framing: compared to a naive deployment without batching/caching/reservation, early optimizations typically drive 40–60% reduction in monthly inference spend for chat workloads.

Attachments: Redwood_TCO_Summary_Q2-2026.pdf (one‑page with table + example calc), ACME_sample-pricing-sheet.xlsx (detailed per‑model/per‑tier math).

Proposed next steps
- I’ll send a detailed per‑model per‑M token breakdown (attached). Can you confirm the monthly sessions estimate (we used 500k) and average session lengths?
- If the numbers look right, let’s schedule a 30‑min procurement + architecture sync next week to review reserved pricing and SSO/KMS questions. Rafael will help with the deployment/ops checklist.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole

Thanks Samir — answers inline and attached the one‑pager/SOW stub. Quick bullets: 

Hosted vs Reserved unit assumptions (used in attachment)
- Hosted (pay‑as‑you–go): $3.00 per 1M tokens (example rate for curated open models on Redwood hosted).
- Dedicated / Reserved (12‑mo): $2.00 per 1M tokens (example committed rate; exact depends on capacity and model mix).

How we model batching savings
- Baseline: per‑token cost derived from measured GPU throughput at small batch sizes. We simulate your request mix (short chat prompts, mid‑length responses) and then model continuous batching gains by increasing effective batch occupancy. For typical chat throughput patterns we see 20–40% reduction in effective per‑token cost; we used 30% in the one‑pager to be conservative.

Example monthly TCO (attached math) — restating with numbers for clarity
- Sessions: 500k/month; tokens/session: 520 => 260M tokens raw.
- Hosted raw @ $3/M: $780/month.
- After batching (30% savings) => 182M equivalent tokens => $546/month hosted.
- After caching (25% further reduction on prompts for multi‑turn flows) => ~136M => $408/month hosted.
- Reserved @ $2/M on the optimized token estimate => 136 * $2 = $272/month.

Notes: the per‑M prices above are illustrative. The attached pricing sheet includes tiering (volume bands), GPU mix assumptions, and a simple sensitivity table so you can slide session volumes and see outcomes.

Attached: Redwood_TCO_Summary_Q2-2026.pdf (one‑pager) — ACME_sample-pricing-sheet.xlsx (detailed calc) — SOW_stub.docx (SOW stub).

Next steps proposed
- Confirm session volume & avg tokens/session.
- Schedule 30m procurement + infra sync (Rafael will run the deployment requirements checklist).
- If procurement is happy, we can run a 30‑day pilot on dedicated capacity to validate savings.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite — thanks.

Marissa
